summary: If someone leaves a jug in the street and another person trips on it and breaks it, he does not pay. If the person who tripped gets hurt, the jug's owner must pay.

chunks.en: Someone who puts a jug in the street,
chunks.st: In the case of one who places a kad, a type of vessel, in the public domain

chunks.en: and another person comes, trips on it, and breaks it,
chunks.st: and another person comes and stumbles on it and breaks it,

chunks.en: does not pay. And if he got hurt by it,
chunks.st: the other person is exempt from paying for what he broke. And if the one who stumbled incurred damaged by it,

chunks.en: the owner of the barrel must pay for his hurt.
chunks.st: the owner of the ḥavit, a type of vessel, is liable to pay restitution for his damage.

chunks.en: If his jug broke in the street,
chunks.st: If one’s jug broke in the public domain and another person

chunks.en: and someone slipped on the water,
chunks.st: slipped in the water from the jug and was injured from the fall,

chunks.en: or was hurt by its broken pieces,
chunks.st: or if he was injured by the shards of the broken jug,

chunks.en: he must pay. Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: the owner of the jug is liable. Rabbi Yehuda says: In a case where the owner of the jug acted

chunks.en: If he meant to, he must pay.
chunks.explain: If he meant to pick up the pieces, he pays.
chunks.st: with intent, he is liable,

chunks.en: If he did not mean to, he does not pay.
chunks.st: and in a case where he acted without intent, he is exempt.

summary: Someone who pours water in the street, or hides thorns or glass, or has a thorn fence or a fence that falls into the street, must pay if people get hurt.

chunks.en: Someone who pours water in the street,
chunks.st: In the case of one who pours water in the public domain,

chunks.en: and another person got hurt by it,
chunks.st: and another person in-curred damage due to it,

chunks.en: must pay for his hurt.
chunks.st: the one who poured water is liable to pay for his damage.

chunks.en: Someone who hides a thorn
chunks.st: In the case of one who conceals a thorn

chunks.en: or glass,
chunks.st: or a piece of glass
chunks.stMore: in his wall adjacent to the public domain,

chunks.en: or makes his fence with thorns,
chunks.st: or one who puts up a fence of thorns,

chunks.en: or a fence that fell into the street,
chunks.st: or one who puts up a fence that subsequently fell into the public domain,

chunks.en: and others got hurt by them,
chunks.st: and others incurred damage due to any of these,

chunks.en: he must pay for their hurt.
chunks.st: he is liable to pay for their damage.

summary: If someone puts straw out in the street and people get hurt, he must pay, and anyone may take it. Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says the same for anyone who blocks the street.

chunks.en: Someone who takes out his straw and
chunks.st: In the case of one who takes out his straw [teven] and

chunks.en: his hay to the street to make fertilizer,
chunks.st: his hay [kash] to the public domain to use afterward as fertilizer

chunks.en: and another person got hurt by them,
chunks.st: and another person incurred damage due to them,

chunks.en: must pay for his hurt,
chunks.st: he is liable to pay for his damage,

chunks.en: and whoever takes them first gets them.
chunks.st: and whoever takes possession of the hay and straw first acquires them for himself.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says,
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

chunks.en: All who make a mess in the street that does damage
chunks.st: With regard to anyone who places obstacles in the public domain and they cause damage,

chunks.en: must pay,
chunks.st: he is liable to pay damages,

chunks.en: and whoever takes them first gets them.
chunks.st: and whoever takes possession of them first acquires them.

chunks.en: Someone who turns over dung in the street,
chunks.st: In the case of one who turns over dung in the public domain

chunks.en: and another person got hurt by it,
chunks.st: and another person incurred damage due to it,

chunks.en: must pay for his hurt.
chunks.st: the former is liable to pay for his damage.

summary: Two potters were walking one behind the other. The first tripped and fell, and the second tripped over him. The first one must pay for the second one's damage.

chunks.en: Two potters who were walking
chunks.st: In the case of two potters carrying pots who were walking

chunks.en: one after the other,
chunks.st: one after the other in the public domain,

chunks.en: and the first tripped and fell,
chunks.st: and the first stumbled on a bump and fell,

chunks.en: and the second tripped over the first,
chunks.st: and the second stumbled over the first and fell too,

chunks.en: the first must pay for the second one's damage.
chunks.st: the first is liable to pay for the damage incurred by the second.

summary: One person carries a barrel and another carries a beam. Who pays if the barrel breaks? It depends on who walked first and who stopped.

chunks.en: This one comes with his barrel,
chunks.st: If this person came in the public domain with his barrel,

chunks.en: and that one comes with his beam,
chunks.st: and that person came from the opposite direction with his cross beam,

chunks.en: and this one's jug broke
chunks.st: and this one’s jug was broken

chunks.en: on that one's beam,
chunks.st: by that one’s cross beam, the one carrying the cross beam is

chunks.he: פָּטוּר, שֶׁלָּזֶה רְשׁוּת לְהַלֵּךְ וְלָזֶה רְשׁוּת לְהַלֵּךְ.
chunks.en: he does not pay, because this one may walk there, and that one may walk there.
chunks.st: exempt, because this one had permission to walk in the public domain, and that one also had permission to walk there.

chunks.en: If the beam carrier was first,
chunks.st: If they were walking in the same direction, so that the owner of the cross beam was walking first, in front,

chunks.en: and the barrel carrier was last,
chunks.st: and the owner of a barrel last, behind him, and

chunks.en: and the barrel broke on the beam,
chunks.st: the barrel was broken by the cross beam,

chunks.en: the beam carrier does not pay.
chunks.st: the owner of the cross beam is exempt,
chunks.stMore: since the owner of the barrel saw him in front of him and should have been more careful.

chunks.en: But if the beam carrier stopped,
chunks.st: But if the owner of the cross beam stopped, causing the barrel to collide with the beam and break,

chunks.he: חַיָּב. וְאִם אָמַר לְבַעַל הֶחָבִית עֲמֹד,
chunks.en: he must pay. And if he told the barrel carrier, "Stop!"
chunks.st: the former is liable,
chunks.stMore: since the latter had no way of anticipating that he would stop. And if he said to the owner of the barrel: Stop,

chunks.en: he does not pay. If the barrel carrier was first
chunks.st: he is exempt from liability for breaking the barrel. Conversely, if the owner of the barrel was walking first

chunks.en: and the beam carrier was last,
chunks.st: and the owner of the cross beam last,

chunks.en: and the barrel broke on the beam,
chunks.st: and the barrel was broken by the cross beam,

chunks.en: he must pay. And if the barrel carrier stopped,
chunks.st: the owner of the cross beam is liable. But if owner of the barrel stopped,

chunks.he: פָּטוּר. וְאִם אָמַר לְבַעַל קוֹרָה עֲמֹד,
chunks.en: he does not pay. And if he told the beam carrier, "Stop!"
chunks.st: the owner of the cross beam is exempt from liability for breaking the barrel. And if he said to the owner of the cross beam: Stop,

chunks.he: חַיָּב. וְכֵן זֶה בָא בְנֵרוֹ וְזֶה בְפִשְׁתָּנוֹ:
chunks.en: he must pay. The same is true if one comes with his candle and one with his flax.
chunks.explain: Flax is a plant that catches fire easily.
chunks.st: the owner of the cross beam is liable. And similarly, these halakhot apply in a case where this one came with his lamp and that one came with his flax, and the lamp set fire to the flax.

summary: Two people walking or running in the street who hurt each other do not have to pay.

chunks.en: Two people who were walking in the street,
chunks.st: With regard to two people who were walking in the public domain,

chunks.en: one running and one walking,
chunks.st: or one who was running and another one who was walking,

chunks.en: or both of them were running,
chunks.st: or who were both running,

chunks.en: and they hurt each other,
chunks.st: and they damaged one another,

chunks.en: both of them do not pay.
chunks.st: both of them are exempt.

summary: Someone chopping wood who makes a chip fly and do damage on someone else's land or in the street must pay.

chunks.he: הַמְבַקֵּעַ בִּרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד וְהִזִּיק בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים,
chunks.en: Someone chopping wood on his own land who did damage in the street,
chunks.st: With regard to one who was chopping wood in his private property and a chip flew off and caused damage in the public property,

chunks.en: or in the street and did damage on private land,
chunks.st: or one who was chopping wood in the public property and caused damage in the private property of another,

chunks.he: בִּרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד וְהִזִּיק בִּרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד אַחֵר, חַיָּב:
chunks.en: or on his own land and did damage on another person's land, must pay.
chunks.st: or one who was chopping wood in his private property and caused damage in the private property of another, in all these cases he is liable.

summary: When two oxen (or people) hurt each other, we see which one did more damage, and that owner pays for the difference: full if mu'ad, half if tam. Rabbi Akiva says a tam ox that hurts a person pays full.

chunks.en: Two tam oxen that hurt
chunks.st: With regard to two innocuous oxen that injured

chunks.en: each other,
chunks.st: each other,

chunks.en: pay half damage for the extra amount.
chunks.explain: Only the one that did more damage pays, for the difference.
chunks.st: the respective damages are evaluated, and if one amount is more than the other, the owner pays half the damages with regard to the difference.
chunks.stMore: In other words, the owner of the ox that caused the greater damage pays the other owner half the difference.

chunks.en: If both are mu'ad,
chunks.st: If both oxen were forewarned,

chunks.en: they pay full damage for the extra.
chunks.st: the owner of the ox that caused the greater damage pays the full cost of the damage with regard to the difference.

chunks.en: One tam and one mu'ad:
chunks.st: In a case where one of the oxen was innocuous and the other one was forewarned,

chunks.he: מוּעָד בַּתָּם מְשַׁלֵּם בַּמּוֹתָר נֶזֶק שָׁלֵם,
chunks.en: a mu'ad that hurt a tam pays full damage for the extra,
chunks.st: if the forewarned ox caused greater damage to the innocuous ox than the reverse, the owner of the forewarned ox pays the full cost of the damage with regard to the difference.

chunks.he: תָּם בַּמּוּעָד מְשַׁלֵּם בַּמּוֹתָר חֲצִי נֶזֶק.
chunks.en: a tam that hurt a mu'ad pays half damage for the extra.
chunks.st: If the innocuous ox caused greater damage to the forewarned ox, its owner pays half the damage with regard to the difference.

chunks.he: וְכֵן שְׁנֵי אֲנָשִׁים שֶׁחָבְלוּ זֶה בָזֶה,
chunks.en: And so too, two people who hurt each other
chunks.st: And similarly, with regard to two people who injured each other,

chunks.en: pay full damage for the extra.
chunks.st: the one who did greater damage pays the full cost of the damage with regard to the difference,
chunks.stMore: since one is always considered forewarned with regard to damage he causes.

chunks.en: A person and a mu'ad ox that hurt each other,
chunks.st: If a person caused damage to a forewarned ox and the forewarned ox caused damage to the person,

chunks.en: pay full damage for the extra.
chunks.st: whichever side caused the greater damage pays the full cost of the damage with regard to the difference.

chunks.en: A person and a tam ox that hurt each other:
chunks.st: In a case where a person caused damage to an innocuous ox and the innocuous ox caused damage to the person,

chunks.he: אָדָם בְּתָם מְשַׁלֵּם בַּמּוֹתָר נֶזֶק שָׁלֵם,
chunks.en: a person who hurt a tam pays full damage for the extra,
chunks.st: if the person caused greater financial damage to the innocuous ox he pays the full cost of the damage with regard to the difference.

chunks.he: תָּם בְּאָדָם מְשַׁלֵּם בַּמּוֹתָר חֲצִי נֶזֶק.
chunks.en: a tam that hurt a person pays half damage for the extra.
chunks.st: If the innocuous ox caused greater damage to the person, its owner pays only half the damage with regard to the difference.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva says:

chunks.en: even a tam that hurt a person
chunks.st: The owner of the innocuous ox that injured a person

chunks.en: pays full damage for the extra.
chunks.st: also pays the full cost of the damage with regard to the difference.
chunks.stMore: Rabbi Akiva does not distinguish between an innocuous and a forewarned ox in a case where an ox injures a person.

summary: When one ox kills another, the Torah says to sell the live ox and split the money, and split the dead one too. Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda disagree about which case the pasuk is talking about.

chunks.en: An ox worth a maneh that gored
chunks.explain: A maneh is one hundred zuz, a lot of money.
chunks.st: With regard to an innocuous ox worth one hundred dinars that gored

chunks.en: an ox worth two hundred,
chunks.st: an ox worth two hundred dinars,

chunks.en: and the dead body is not worth anything,
chunks.st: and the carcass of the dead ox is not worth anything,

words.note: The body of an animal that died.

chunks.en: the owner takes the ox.
chunks.st: its owner takes the entire ox that gored it,
chunks.stMore: since it is worth half the value of the damage.

chunks.en: An ox worth two hundred that gored
chunks.st: With regard to an innocuous ox worth two hundred dinars that gored

chunks.en: an ox worth two hundred,
chunks.st: another ox worth two hundred,

chunks.en: and the dead body is not worth anything,
chunks.st: and the carcass is worth nothing,

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir said:

chunks.en: About this the Torah says, "They shall sell
chunks.st: It is about this type of case that it is stated: “Then they shall sell

chunks.he: אֶת הַשּׁוֹר הַחַי וְחָצוּ אֶת כַּסְפּוֹ.
chunks.en: the live ox and split its money."
chunks.st: the live ox, and divide its monetary value” (Exodus 21:35).

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda said to him,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda said to him:

chunks.en: That is the halacha,
chunks.explain: Rabbi Yehuda agrees with the ruling, not the reason.
chunks.st: And that is the halakha, yet your interpretation of the verse is incorrect.

chunks.en: but you kept "They shall sell the ox,
chunks.st: You have upheld the clause: “

chunks.en: the live one and split its money,"
chunks.st: Then they shall sell the live ox and divide its monetary value,” which fits your interpretation of the case.

chunks.en: and you did not keep, "And also
chunks.st: But you have not upheld the latter clause of the verse: “

chunks.en: the dead one they shall split."
chunks.explain: In your case the dead ox is worth nothing to split.
chunks.st: And the dead they shall also divide,” since in the case you mentioned the carcass is worthless.

chunks.en: Which case is it? An ox worth two hundred
chunks.st: Rather, to which case is the verse referring? It is the case of an ox worth two hundred dinars

chunks.en: that gored an ox worth two hundred,
chunks.st: that gored another ox worth two hundred dinars,

chunks.en: and the dead body is worth fifty zuz.
chunks.st: and the carcass is worth fifty dinars.

chunks.he: שֶׁזֶּה נוֹטֵל חֲצִי הַחַי וַחֲצִי הַמֵּת,
chunks.en: This one takes half the live one and half the dead one,
chunks.st: In this case, this party takes half the value of the living ox, one hundred dinars, and half the value of the dead ox, twenty-five dinars;

chunks.he: וְזֶה נוֹטֵל חֲצִי הַחַי וַחֲצִי הַמֵּת:
chunks.en: and that one takes half the live one and half the dead one.
chunks.st: and that party also takes half the value of the living ox and half the value of the dead ox.

summary: Sometimes a person pays for what his ox did but not for what he did himself, and sometimes the other way around. The mishnah gives examples.

chunks.en: Sometimes one must pay for what his ox did
chunks.st: There are cases where one is liable for an act of damage caused by his ox,

chunks.en: but not for what he did himself;
chunks.st: but exempt from liability for the same action if he performed it himself.

chunks.en: or does not pay for what his ox did
chunks.st: Conversely, there are also cases where one is exempt from liability for the action of his ox,

chunks.en: but must pay for what he did himself.
chunks.st: but liable for his own action.

chunks.en: If his ox embarrassed someone,
chunks.st: How so? If his ox caused a person humilation,

chunks.en: he does not pay; but if he embarrassed someone,
chunks.st: he is exempt from paying compensation, but if he himself humiliated another,

chunks.he: חַיָּב. שׁוֹרוֹ שֶׁסִּמֵּא אֶת עֵין עַבְדּוֹ,
chunks.en: he pays. If his ox blinded the eye of his servant,
chunks.st: he is liable. Similarly, if his ox blinded the eye of his slave

chunks.en: or knocked out his tooth,
chunks.st: or knocked out his slave’s tooth,

chunks.he: פָּטוּר, וְהוּא שֶׁסִּמֵּא אֶת עֵין עַבְדּוֹ,
chunks.en: he does not have to free him. But if he blinded his servant's eye,
chunks.explain: A master who hurts his servant this way must set him free.
chunks.st: he is exempt from having to emancipate the slave for this mutilation. But if he himself blinded his slave’s eye

chunks.en: or knocked out his tooth,
chunks.st: or knocked out his tooth,

chunks.en: he must free him. If his ox hurt his father or mother,
chunks.st: he is liable to emancipate him, as stated in the Torah (Exodus 21:26–27). By contrast, if his ox injured the owner’s father or his mother,

chunks.en: he pays; but if he hurt his father or mother,
chunks.st: he is liable to pay damages, but if he himself injured his father or his mother,

chunks.he: פָּטוּר. שׁוֹרוֹ שֶׁהִדְלִיק אֶת הַגָּדִישׁ בְּשַׁבָּת,
chunks.en: he does not pay. If his ox set a pile of grain on fire on Shabbos,
chunks.st: he is exempt from paying compensation. Similarly, if his ox set fire to a haystack on Shabbat,

chunks.he: חַיָּב, וְהוּא שֶׁהִדְלִיק אֶת הַגָּדִישׁ בְּשַׁבָּת,
chunks.en: he pays; but if he set a pile on fire on Shabbos,
chunks.st: he is liable to pay damages. But if he himself set fire to a haystack on Shabbat,

chunks.en: he does not pay, because he gets a much bigger punishment.
chunks.explain: He is punished by beis din, so he does not also pay.
chunks.st: he is exempt from paying damages. He is exempt from payment in these cases due to the fact that he is liable to receive the death penalty for injuring his father or mother or for desecrating Shabbat.

summary: When we do not know which ox did the damage, or which kind of ox did it, the one who wants to take money from the other must bring proof.

chunks.he: שׁוֹר שֶׁהָיָה רוֹדֵף אַחַר שׁוֹר אַחֵר,
chunks.en: An ox was chasing another ox,
chunks.st: With regard to an ox that was pursuing another ox, and the ox being pursued

chunks.en: and it got hurt. This one says, "Your ox did damage,"
chunks.st: became injured, but there are no witnesses as to how it was injured, and this one, the owner of the injured ox, says to the owner of the pursuing ox: Your ox injured my ox, and you are liable to pay me damages,

chunks.en: and that one says, "No,
chunks.st: and that one, the owner of the pursuing ox, says in response:

chunks.en: it was hurt by a rock."
chunks.st: No; rather, it was hurt by a rock, and I am not liable, then in this case,

chunks.en: Whoever wants to take money from his friend must bring proof.
chunks.st: the burden of proof rests upon the claimant.
chunks.stMore: As long as the owner of the injured ox cannot prove that the injury was inflicted by the pursuing ox, the owner of the pursuing ox is not liable.

chunks.en: If two oxen were chasing one ox,
chunks.st: In a case where two oxen, belonging to two different owners, were pursuing one ox belonging to a third person, and that ox was injured by one of the pursuing oxen,

chunks.en: this one says, "Your ox did damage,"
chunks.st: and this one, the owner of one of the pursuing oxen, says to the owner of the other: It was your ox that caused the injury,

chunks.en: and that one says, "Your ox did damage,"
chunks.st: and that one, the owner of the other pursuing ox, says: No, it was your ox that caused the injury,

chunks.en: both of them do not pay.
chunks.st: the two of them are exempt,
chunks.stMore: since each of them rejects the claim of the injured party that his ox caused the injury.

chunks.he: אִם הָיוּ שְׁנֵיהֶן שֶׁל אִישׁ אֶחָד,
chunks.en: If both belonged to one man,
chunks.st: If both oxen belonged to one person,

chunks.en: both must pay.
chunks.st: both are liable, as will be explained in the Gemara.

chunks.en: If one was big and one was small,
chunks.st: If the pursuing oxen both belonged to one person, and were both innocuous, so that restitution is paid exclusively from proceeds of the sale of the belligerent ox, and one was large and the other one small,

chunks.en: the one who was hurt says the big one did damage,
chunks.st: in this case, if the injured party says that the large ox caused the damage, and he is therefore entitled to receive restitution for half the damage from the value of the large ox,

chunks.en: and the damager says, "No,
chunks.st: but the one liable for damage says: No;

chunks.en: the small one did damage."
chunks.st: rather, the small ox caused the damage, and half of its value is not sufficient to cover half the damage;

chunks.en: One tam and one mu'ad:
chunks.st: or, similarly, in a case where one ox is innocuous and one is forewarned,

chunks.en: the one who was hurt says,
chunks.st: and the injured party says: The

chunks.en: "The mu'ad did damage,"
chunks.st: forewarned ox caused the damage, and the injured party is therefore eligible to receive full damages,

chunks.en: and the damager says, "No,
chunks.st: but the one liable for damage says: No; rather, the

chunks.en: the tam did damage."
chunks.st: innocuous ox caused the damage, in which case he is liable to pay only half the damage;

chunks.en: Whoever wants to take money from his friend must bring proof.
chunks.st: in both of the above cases, the principle is that the burden of proof rests upon the claimant.

chunks.en: If the ones that got hurt were two,
chunks.st: If the injured animals were two oxen,

chunks.en: one big and one small,
chunks.st: one large and the other one small,

chunks.en: and the ones that did damage were two,
chunks.st: and the ones that caused the damage were also two oxen,

chunks.en: one big and one small,
chunks.st: one large and one small,

chunks.en: the one who was hurt says,
chunks.st: and the injured party says:

chunks.en: "The big one hurt the big one,
chunks.st: The large one injured the large one

chunks.en: and the small one hurt the small one,"
chunks.st: and the small one injured the small one,

chunks.en: and the damager says, "No,
chunks.st: and the one liable for damage says: No;

chunks.en: the small one hurt the big one,
chunks.st: rather, the small one injured the large one,
chunks.stMore: in which case, if half the value of the belligerent ox does not cover half the damage, he is not required to pay more,

chunks.en: and the big one hurt the small one."
chunks.st: and the large one injured the small one;

chunks.en: One tam and one mu'ad:
chunks.st: or, similarly, if one of the belligerent oxen was innocuous and one forewarned,

chunks.en: the one who was hurt says,
chunks.st: and the injured party says: The

chunks.en: "The mu'ad hurt the big one,
chunks.st: forewarned ox injured the large one,

chunks.en: and the tam hurt the small one,"
chunks.st: and the innocuous ox injured the small one,

chunks.en: and the damager says, "No,
